body.statement:
There are constants \(n_0\in\mathbb N\) and \(C_L<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\), such that, for \(n\ge n_0\), choose \((h,k)\) by deterministic minimization of \(B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\) over \(h\le r_0\), \(1\le k\le m h^d\), and \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\).  For any deterministic pilot spline dimensions \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\),
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}\{C_n(h,k)\}]
 \le C_L r_{\mathrm{up}},
\]
where \(r_{\mathrm{up}}\) uses \(\bar q=\min\{q,\gamma\}\) as in the corrected phase-rate definition.  Thus the length of this global-sensitivity construction is governed by the privacy-free term, the ordinary private-regression term, and a higher-order term which equals the \(q\)-branch for \(q<\gamma\) and the private-Gram branch \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}\) for \(q\ge\gamma\).  No matching full-class lower claim is made.
body.justification: The result gives the first auditable privacy phase diagram for the length, rather than only asymptotic validity of a private causal interval.
body.gap: ShohamEtAl2026 gives a black-box asymptotic resampling interval, and SchroederHartensteinFeuerriegel2025 gives a regular ATE interval; neither derives a pointwise Hölder CATE expected-length phase.
body.consumer: Study designers can select bandwidth, higher-order dimension, and privacy budget to meet a prespecified interval-width requirement.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\ell=h k^{-1/d}\).  Because \(1\le k\le m h^d\),
\[
 m^{-1/d}\le \ell\le h\le r_0\le\frac14.
\]
The definitions, \(m\asymp n\), and \(\sqrt{a+b}\le\sqrt a+\sqrt b\) give, with constants depending only on the displayed fixed quantities and \(\eta\),
\[
\begin{split}
 B(h,k)&\lesssim h^\gamma+\ell^q,\\
 S(h,k,\eta)&\lesssim n^{-1/2}h^{-d/2}
       +n^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2},\\
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)&\lesssim
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-d}
       +N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-d}\ell^{-d}.
\end{split}
\]
Indeed, \(h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\le h^\gamma\), \(\sqrt{k}=h^{d/2}\ell^{-d/2}\), and \(k h^{-2d}=h^{-d}\ell^{-d}\).  The two logarithms in the definition of \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}\) differ from those in \(G\) only by a factor depending on the fixed \(\eta\).

Let
\[
 r_o=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},\qquad
 r_2=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2q))}.
\]
Direct comparison of their exponents at
\(q=d/\{2(1+d/(2\gamma))\}\) shows that
\(r_{\mathrm{np}}=r_o\vee r_2\).  Put
\(t=r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}}\), with the corrected \(r_{\mathrm{ho}}\).

First suppose \(q<\gamma\) and \(t\) is smaller than a fixed constant.  Choose, up to fixed multiplicative constants,
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\qquad \ell=t^{1/q},\qquad
 k=(h/\ell)^d,
\]
rounding \(k\) to a positive integer.  Integer rounding changes every displayed order only by a fixed factor.  The inequalities \(t\ge r_o,r_2,r_{\mathrm{reg}},r_{\mathrm{ho}}\) are respectively equivalent to
\[
 n^{-1/2}t^{-d/(2\gamma)}\le t,
 \quad n^{-1}t^{-d/(2\gamma)-d/(2q)}\le t,
 \quad N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma}\le t,
 \quad N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma-d/q}\le t.
\]
They bound all four fluctuation terms, while \(h^\gamma=\ell^q=t\).

The rank restriction also holds for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Indeed, \(\epsilon_n\le1\), \(\delta_n<1/2\), and \(\eta<1/4\) imply \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}\le C_\eta n\).  If
\(a_{\mathrm{ho}}=1/(1+d/\gamma+d/q)\), then
\(a_{\mathrm{ho}}\le q/d\).  Hence \(t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}\gtrsim n^{-q/d}\), so \(\ell=t^{1/q}\gtrsim n^{-1/d}\), which is equivalent, up to the harmless factor between \(m\) and \(n\), to \(k\le m h^d\).  Also \(m h^d\to\infty\), so the stated local-sample constraint eventually holds.

If \(q\ge\gamma\), take \(k=1\), so \(\ell=h\), and take \(h=t^{1/\gamma}\).  Then \(\ell^q\le h^\gamma=t\).  The first sampling term is bounded because \(t\ge r_o\), and the second is its square and is therefore no larger for sufficiently large \(n\).  The leading privacy term is now
\(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-2d}\); the corrected formula gives
\(r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+2d/\gamma)}\), so this term is at most \(t\).  The remaining privacy term is smaller.  This also proves why replacing \(q\) by \(\bar q=\min\{q,\gamma\}\) is necessary.

If \(t\) is bounded below by a fixed constant, any feasible choice suffices because \(C_n(h,k)\subset[-1,1]\) and hence its length is at most two.  For \(n\ge n_0\), the feasible set is nonempty and compact after restricting \(h\) by the displayed local-sample inequality; since \(k\) ranges over finitely many integers, a minimizer exists.  Its radius is no larger than the radius at the preceding candidate.  Finally,
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{C_n(h,k)\}\le 2R_n(h,k)
\]
deterministically.  Taking expectations and the supremum over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) proves the result.  The proof concerns length only and does not use the unresolved stochastic-remainder assertion.
